core.title: Give each mapped-pair plan artifact an executable bar on its mapped metric
core.given: A plan artifact under the configured plan root carries a dimension+direction pair that the dimension->metric mapping resolves to a metric id.
core.when: You create or edit that plan artifact or its acceptances, or a corpus-wide check inspects it (existing, unchanged plan artifacts under the plan root included).
core.then: An acceptance (one suffices) states an executable bar: its signal.metric equals the mapping's metric id for that pair, and its signal.threshold is one the evaluation can actually evaluate (a present field alone is not a bar).
prefer: Resolve the pair through the mapping before writing the bar: down (minimize|decrease) / up (maximize|increase), all metric ids metric:-prefixed - time latency_p50/latency_increase; effort user_steps/unmapped; likelihood error_ratio/success_ratio; frequency occurrence_rate/unmapped; quantity scrap_rate/throughput; financial value cost_per_unit/net_margin.
Use the plan-artifact schema's exact dimension/direction spelling; minimize=decrease and maximize=increase resolve to the same metric id.
Copy the metric id verbatim, prefix included.
avoid: A mapped-pair plan artifact under the plan root with no bar, a metric other than the mapped one, a threshold that cannot be evaluated, or a bar dropped on edit.
Reading the advisory disposition as permission never to add the bar - the debt is paid deliberately, in phases.
core.why: A dimension+direction is testable only once it names a metric and an evaluable threshold.
evidence: A corpus check lists mapped plan artifacts lacking an executable bar, with failure evidence: the artifact's urn, dimension, direction, metric id, cause.

A reviewer traverses the plan artifact's acceptances to each signal and confirms the signal's metric equals the mapping's metric id and the threshold is one the evaluation can actually evaluate (not just a present field).
verification: Scope: authoring (create/edit of the plan artifact or its acceptances) and the corpus inspection alike apply only to plan artifacts under the configured plan root, scanned recursively; mapped plan artifacts outside the plan root are out of scope.

Enforced as an advisory corpus check (severity 2 in the reference realization): it scans plan artifacts under the plan root, recursively, whose dimension+direction the mapping resolves, traverses each artifact's acceptances to its signal, and reports artifacts that state no executable bar naming the assigned metric id, with failure evidence: artifact urn, dimension, direction, metric id, cause.

Advisory means the check reports the debt rather than failing on it (in the reference realization the whole mapped corpus would fail on day one and some mapped metrics have no evaluator yet); the disposition is not permission never to add the bar - the debt is paid deliberately, in phases.
Executability is judged against the stack's bar evaluation: a threshold that is present but never evaluated does not satisfy the bar.

The check does not cover pairs the mapping leaves unmapped (such a plan artifact must state its own metric - separate rule), changes limited to the mapping table or the plan-artifact schema enums (separate rule), or artifacts carrying no dimension/direction at all.

fires: A planner creates a plan artifact under the plan root with time/minimize (mapped to metric:latency_p50), before or after acceptances exist
A planner edits a likelihood/increase plan artifact under the plan root whose bar names metric:success_ratio - the bar must survive the edit
The corpus check finds an unchanged quantity/maximize plan artifact under the plan root with no signal metric/threshold - reported (advisory)
A mapped-pair plan artifact's signal names a different metric, or its threshold cannot be evaluated - the bar must be repaired
doesNotFire: A plan artifact on effort or frequency with maximize/increase (unmapped) - see .unmapped-pair-own-metric
Editing only the dimension->metric mapping or the plan-artifact schema enums - see .table-totality
A mapped-pair plan artifact outside the configured plan root - the rule's scope is plan artifacts under the plan root
Product code, docs or other non-plan artifacts with no plan-artifact dimension/direction

profileRequirements.meaning: The configured plan root: the core scopes the whole obligation (authoring and corpus inspection) to plan artifacts under this root, and the corpus check scans that root recursively; the core expresses the recursion, the profile supplies only the root path.

The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role (the Bun check's validation.subject_kind and the activation's file_kind value, a one-kind list in the reference realization); the check's subject kind and the activation's file kind resolve to one of these.
What the stack calls a plan artifact, wherever the core says 'plan artifact'.

neutralityNotes: The plan-artifact layer's own vocabulary - the dimension/direction enums, acceptances[].signal.metric / signal.threshold, the metric: id scheme, the dimension->metric table's content, the SMOKE phase, and the sibling rule ids (.unmapped-pair-own-metric, .table-totality) - is ATDD methodology shared across stacks, not stack structure, so it stays in the core verbatim rather than becoming profile data or bunOnly. Scope (audit round 2): Bun's plan/** selector is decomposed into the profile's plan-root path (roots.plan = 'plan', a path, not a glob) plus a core-expressed recursive restriction - the given, when, file_kind activation fact, fires, a doesNotFire entry and the verification entry all limit the obligation, for authoring and corpus inspection alike, to plan artifacts under the configured plan root; the profile supplies only where plan artifacts live (roots.plan), what the stack calls them (roles.plan_artifact.name = 'DESIRED OUTCOME') and which concrete kinds play the role (roles.plan_artifact.kinds = 'desired outcome', Bun's validation.subject_kind / file_kind value; a one-kind list in the reference realization). Realization state that could not be neutralized - validator/test ids, the metric_runner.py module inventory, evaluator function passes(), and the corpus statistics (472/368/102, govern_lifecycle/D010) and histories (#1958/#1959/#1925) - is carried in bunOnly. 'Product capabilities' in doesNotFire was rendered as generic non-plan product code/docs. Per rule 7, this rule's severity (2) and advisory disposition live in core verification, not in the profile.
